new_statements.rule_in_words: Caijia (Xingfa variety) is described as a lexical-tone language: five citation tones (55, 33, 22, 21, 24), four surface tones, tone sandhi and derivational tone change. The grammar gives no word-stress placement rule and no section on stress/accent; stress is mentioned only as a sentence-level prosodic factor that can raise the surface pitch of a morpheme (pʰa 'pat'; completive ha⁵⁵ realised [51] 'when it is stressed').
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal notes: low-level /22/ usually surfaces as [21]; /33/ -> [21] before /55/ obligatorily; free variation /33/~[21] after /55/ and /21/~[33] before /21/; plural pronouns and diminutives derived by tone change to [24].
new_statements.domain_note: The two stress remarks concern emphasis within sentences/connected texts, not lexical word stress; citation forms are monosyllabic tone-bearing morphemes. Author explicitly says the chapter is 'a brief description of the sound system' and does not explore phonology in depth.
new_statements.identity_note: Lü 2020/2022 describes the Xingfa 兴发乡 variety of Hezhang County (with occasional notes on the Weining/Xinfa variety); Hsiu 2018 describes the Niujiaojing (Yangjie, Weining) dialect. All are caij1234 (no sub-glottocodes). Caijia has no ISO code.
